answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity a costly, long-lived asset: an agent must stake real collateral that is slashed if its attestations are graded as junk. Like an orchard, trust grows slowly from verified seasons of honest work, and no shortcut lets a thousand fresh clones inherit that yield overnight. A sybil farmer would need to fund every fake seat at full price, watching that ember of capital burn with no return, while established identities stay clean as ivory under continuous peer grading.
